plan: This mechanism is equivalent to a second-price sealed-bid auction: the winner pays the second-highest bid, and my exit price is my own sealed bid. Bidding above or below my true value only risks winning at a loss or missing profitable wins. Therefore, bidding exactly my value ($3) is the dominant strategy—it ensures I win only when profitable and never overpay, since I only pay the second-highest bid, not my own.

Since the auction mechanism results in the winner paying the second-highest sealed bid (equivalent to a second-price/Vickrey auction), the dominant strategy is to bid my true value. Bidding truthfully ensures I win whenever my value exceeds others' bids, and I pay less than my value, maximizing expected profit without risk of overpaying.

This auction mechanism effectively functions as a second-price auction: I exit at my sealed bid, and if I win, I pay the second-highest bid. Since my payment doesn't depend on my own bid (only on whether I win and what others bid), bidding my true value is the dominant strategy. Bidding higher risks overpaying relative to my value, and bidding lower risks losing profitable opportunities. Therefore, I will bid exactly my value of $11.
